25.constraint: Use the Air Force blue clean tapered performance jogger once only for Spring or Summer Sports / Workout. Pair with white, ecru, soft gray, restrained olive, or muted navy performance tops and simple technical sneakers; do not add cargo pockets, a bulky layer, or another shiny garment.

38.constraint: Use the brown regular-proportion faux-suede zip jacket once only for Spring or Fall Casual Everyday, Travel, or Date Night. Pair with ecru, white, soft gray, pale blue, stone, or clean dark-indigo straight bottoms; keep the shirt and footwear minimal so the warm jacket remains the single statement.

rejectionGroups.reason: Floating, hanger-only or laid-flat shirt imagery does not prove adult-male shoulder, chest, sleeve, body length, or hem behavior, and these plain shirt roles are already better represented by approved on-body identities.
The hanger-only fleece-lined plaid shirt looks bulky and inexpensive, with saturated checks, gold-tone buttons and no adult fit proof.
The plaid shirt is extremely long and oversized, with dropped shoulders, sleeve volume, multiple visible supplier labels and an uncontrolled layered silhouette.
The close-up product image combines a striped shirt collar with an artificial V-neck cardigan front and never proves the complete adult torso or hem proportion.
The floating shirt uses a dense novelty Nordic-style print, a visible hang tag and no on-body proof, making it costume-led rather than modern and versatile.
The asymmetrical button placement, severe narrow torso and sleeves, high collar and product-only rendering create a dated gimmick shirt.
The on-body shirt is tight through the chest, upper arms and waist, with dated double utility pockets and a short fitted proportion.
The product-only shirt has a narrow synthetic body, tight sleeves and a high stand collar that reads dated formal rather than clean modern.
The half-sleeve shirt is very wide and long, with oversized utility pockets and a conspicuous tan supplier label near the hem.
The inspected black, dark-gray and white shirts use an exaggerated dropped shoulder, long body and wide sleeves; the light option remains shapeless rather than controlled relaxed.
The shirt has an extremely dropped shoulder, oversized sleeve and long body, producing the shapeless baggy-top problem across the visible variants.
The fitted shirt is narrow through the torso and sleeves and repeats the skinny office-shirt proportion being removed.
The trousers are excessively wide or loose and visibly puddle over the shoes; close inspection of the colored variants confirmed the same baggy full-length silhouette.
The synthetic two-tone pant has an uncontrolled wide leg, extended drawstring and repetitive composited travel backgrounds that weaken product trust.
Product-only cropped or loose drawstring trousers provide no adult proof of rise, seat, thigh, knee, hem, or footwear relationship.
The dark active jogger is overloaded with cargo panels, exposed zippers and long drawstrings, creating busy generic gymwear.
Every inspected color has excessive thigh volume and bunches heavily above the elastic cuffs, recreating the baggy jogger problem.
The very wide cropped pant, low crotch and decorative tassel drawstring create a costume-like silhouette rather than a versatile modern bottom.
The product-only jacket mixes contrast denim-look sleeves, brown shoulder panels and diamond quilting in a dated patchwork construction.
The bulky fleece-lined jacket is product-only and carries conspicuous FASHION and sleeve patches with dated contrast stitching.
The washed black faux-leather blazer hybrid has multiple diagonal zippers, flap pockets and a crumpled synthetic finish with no fit proof.
Although relatively clean, the cropped torso view hides the complete hem and lower-body relationship; both variants are repetitive dark navy with a narrow office-jacket proportion.
The otherwise clean product-only knit jacket has no adult fit proof and carries a visible chest brand plate; it does not add enough value over approved layers.
Both faux-leather variants use an excessively tall stand collar, long synthetic body and generic high-street motorcycle finish.
The product-only dark jacket uses loud double shoulder stripes, striped ribbing and a dated generic varsity construction.
The windbreaker is extremely oversized and long with high-contrast panels, elastic bulk and visible chest branding.
The two-tone faux-leather racing jacket has giant NOOPER lettering, high-contrast panels and a narrow dated shape.
The product-only utility jacket is overloaded with chest and lower pockets, epaulettes, stitching and an embroidered pocket emblem, with no fit proof.
The glossy crocodile-texture faux-leather bomber is product-only, bulky, repetitive black and visibly inexpensive.

qaSummary: 40 identities and all 145 recorded color images rendered; 185 displayed images loaded with zero broken files.
2 accepted with one exact color and variant selected: one active bottom and one outerwear identity.
38 rejected after the base pass and close inspection of 16 promising color variants.
Accepted colors are Air Force blue and brown; no top passed because every candidate was skinny, uncontrolled oversized, branded, novelty-led, or lacked reliable fit proof.

Rejections include hanger-only shirts, skinny formal tops, overlong plaid layers, puddled sweatpants, wide cropped trousers, cargo-heavy joggers, patchwork quilting, logo-led fleece, dated racing leather, oversized windbreakers and shiny synthetic bombers.
